title: Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture
formal: For every pair of integers \(n\ge 2\) and \(1\le r\le n- 1\), does every simple loopless digraph D on n vertices with minimum outdegree at least r contain a directed cycle of length at most \(\operatorname{ceil}(n/r)\)?
definitions: A simple loopless digraph has a finite vertex set V and an arc set \(A\subseteq \{(u,v)\in V\times V:u\ne v\}\); each ordered pair occurs at most once. Both \((u,v)\) and \((v,u)\) are allowed. The outdegree \(d^{+}(v)\) is |\(\{u:(v,u)\in A\}|\) and minimum outdegree is \(\min _{v\in V}d^{+}(v)\). A directed cycle of length \(\ell\)\(\ge 2\) is a sequence of pairwise distinct vertices \(v_{1},\ldots ,v_{\ell}\) with \((v_{i},v_{i+1})\in A\) for every i and \(v_{\ell +1}=v_{1}\). Thus an opposite pair of arcs is a directed 2-cycle. \(\operatorname{ceil}(n/r)\) is the least integer not smaller than \(n/r\). There is no planarity, regularity, connectivity or algorithmic assumption.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation with the stated model, hypotheses and quantifier order. The proof must settle the entire target. A result conditional on an additional assumption settles only that conditional version. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof checked by a proof assistant and matching this statement.
why: Determine the sharp universal relationship between a local directed-degree condition and the existence of a short directed cycle.

importance.reason: A central directed-graph conjecture expressing a simple, general degree-versus-girth principle.

references.locator: Discrete Mathematics 349 (2026), 114868; Conjecture 1 and related rainbow-cycle results
references.title: Short rainbow cycles for families of small edge sets

progress.text: Guo’s preprint and journal article state the general conjecture while proving related rainbow-cycle statements.

context_blocks.text: Positive outdegree ensures that some directed cycle exists, but it gives no immediate sharp estimate of its length. The conjecture proposes the threshold \(\operatorname{ceil}(n/r)\) when every vertex has at least r outgoing neighbors.

Allowing opposite arcs makes the graph model a general simple digraph rather than an orientation of a simple graph. The ceiling and minimum-degree quantifiers must be preserved when comparing formulations.

Recent rainbow-cycle research continues to use this directed-girth assertion as an unresolved reference point. A theorem about several colored edge sets does not by itself supply the cycle in every digraph specified here.

sentences: The conjecture links minimum outdegree with the length of a directed cycle.
An n-vertex digraph of minimum outdegree r should contain a cycle of length at most the ceiling of n divided by r.
Opposite arcs are allowed, but loops and parallel copies of an arc are forbidden.
The assertion covers all graphs and all positive degree thresholds in the stated range.
It is a sharp general principle connecting local expansion with global directed cycles.
